dimensions.name: network_calls
dimensions.label: New or changed network calls
dimensions.reasoning: dao/ssl-geospec.js makes an outbound HTTPS GET request to an IP geolocation API (decoded from base64: 'https://api.ipgeolocation.io/ipgeo?apiKey=ae511e1627824a968aaaa758a5309154'). This call is used to determine the victim's country and conditionally trigger destructive file overwrites. The network call is the trigger mechanism for the payload.

dimensions.name: obfuscation
dimensions.label: Obfuscation / encoding patterns (base64, eval, dynamic require)
dimensions.reasoning: dao/ssl-geospec.js is a single minified line with extensive base64 encoding of all significant strings: the API URL ('aHR0cHM6Ly9hcGkuaXBnZW9sb2NhdGlvbi5pby9pcGdlbz9hcGlLZXk9YWU1MTFlMTYyNzgyNGE5NjhhYWFhNzU4YTUzMDkxNTQ='), directory paths ('Li8=', 'Li4v', 'Li4vLi4v', 'Lw=='), field names ('Y291bnRyeV9uYW1l' = 'country_name'), and target country strings ('cnVzc2lh' = 'russia', 'YmVsYXJ1cw==' = 'belarus'). The overwrite payload '4p2k77iP' decodes to a heart emoji. The obfuscation is clearly intentional to hide malicious intent.

dimensions.reasoning: No explicit preinstall/postinstall script changes are visible in the diff. The malicious code is injected via module import in services/IPC.js, so it executes at runtime when the IPC module is used, not at install time.

dimensions.name: env_conditional
dimensions.label: Conditional logic gated on env vars, platform, or CI detection
dimensions.reasoning: The payload in dao/ssl-geospec.js is conditionally triggered based on geographic location (country_name containing 'russia' or 'belarus'). A random delay (Math.ceil(Math.random()*1e3) ms) and a random probability check (Math.round(Math.random()*4) > 1 returns early, so only ~25-50% of executions proceed) are used to make detection harder. This is a nation-state-targeted conditional.

dimensions.name: resource_exhaustion
dimensions.label: Denial-of-service / resource-exhaustion patterns (unbounded loops, recursion, unthrottled blocking calls)
dimensions.reasoning: The function h() is recursive (calls itself for subdirectories), traversing the filesystem from root paths ('./', '../', '../../', '/'). On a large filesystem this could be resource-intensive, but it has a base case (non-directory files) and will terminate. The primary risk here is destructive file overwriting, not resource exhaustion per se.

llm_summary: This is a confirmed malicious supply chain attack in node-ipc 10.1.0→10.1.1. The added file dao/ssl-geospec.js is a deliberately obfuscated wiper payload that: (1) calls an IP geolocation API using a base64-encoded URL, (2) checks if the resolved country is Russia or Belarus, and (3) if so, recursively overwrites all files in './', '../', '../../', and '/' with a heart emoji character. All sensitive strings are base64-encoded to evade detection. The payload is injected via a new import in services/IPC.js and executes on module load with a random delay and probability factor to hinder detection. This matches the well-documented node-ipc protest-ware incident targeting users in Russia and Belarus.
